title: Priv cluster token-binding race causing RBAC denials and missing audit events during control-plane failover
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Summary:
A customer escalated a production failure in a Private cluster running the control plane across three nodes. During a control-plane leader failover while KMS envelope unwraps were in-flight, ephemeral token bindings (node-instance -> session) were not consistently reattached to the new leader. This caused RBAC checks to intermittently fail for valid service sessions and, in several cases, resulted in audit events not being emitted or being written with truncated metadata. The issue surfaced after a routine OS patch and coincided with a transient increase in SAML assertion replay retries from a downstream IdP.

Why this matters:
- Customer-facing APIs experienced 5–10s authorization failures for internal service-to-service requests, leading to degraded feature availability for one customer (high-value enterprise).
- Several audit records for the affected time window are missing the tenant and request_id fields, complicating compliance investigations.
- The failure mode is reproducible in internal staging when simulating multi-node control-plane failovers under concurrent KMS unwrap load and SAML assertion bursts.

Scope:
- Private deployments (VPC/on-prem) using KMS envelope encryption for ephemeral tokens and SSO via SAML. Hosted/Dedicated customers are not affected by the token-binding path in the private control plane.

Reproduction steps (short):
1) Deploy a private control-plane cluster with 3 control-plane instances and KMS backend configured.
2) Create long-lived in-flight operations that require ephemeral token binding to the control-plane instance (e.g., streaming API sessions + background inference calls).
3) Simulate leader failover (systemctl restart control-plane or kill -9 leader process) while concurrently firing SAML assertion replays and KMS unwrap calls.
4) Observe RBAC DENY responses for previously-authorized sessions and audit events missing tenant/request metadata for ~30–90s window.
impact_summary: Intermittent authorization denials (5–10s) for internal requests; missing/truncated audit log metadata for compliance; escalated by one enterprise customer and triggered on-call pager alerts.
mitigation:
Short-term mitigations applied on 2026-03-11:
- Rolled back the OS micro-update on one affected customer cluster (mitigated but not root-cause).
- Added a temporary control-plane admission gate that rejects leader stepdown if more than X unwraps/sec are in-flight (reduces probability of race).
- Customer workaround documented: schedule maintenance windows and avoid simultaneous IdP retries during control-plane restarts.
proposed_fix:
Root cause: race between KMS envelope unwrap callback and the leader election/instance-id rebind path for ephemeral token bindings. Token metadata reattachment relied on an optimistic lookup that assumed unwrap completion preceded leader transition. When ordering flips, tokens were registered to a missing instance id, causing RBAC checks to resolve to an anonymous principal and audit code to skip tenant enrichment.

Fix plan (high level):
1) Change token binding registration to use a robust compare-and-reconcile step: when the new leader mounts, reconcile in-flight unwrap operations by checking KMS unwrap correlation IDs and atomically reconciling token->instance mappings.
2) Ensure audit logging path tolerates temporary instance-id gaps by buffering enrichment metadata for up to 120s and writing full metadata once available; degrade with explicit placeholders rather than dropping fields.
3) Harden SAML retry handling to add jitter and backoff during leader elections to avoid cascading unwrap bursts.
4) Add deterministic unit and e2e tests that simulate leader failover + concurrent unwraps + assertion retries.

Rollout strategy:
- Canary on one low-risk customer private cluster with extended tracing.
- Gradual rollout to remaining clusters with a quick rollback path.
- Add migration job that reconciles historical in-flight tokens for the last 24h (if any).
acceptance_criteria:
- Token bindings survive simulated leader failover with concurrent KMS unwraps in staging (no RBAC DENY for valid sessions).
- Audit events emitted during failover windows contain tenant and request_id fields (no truncation), verified by end-to-end test harness.
- Unit/e2e tests added and green in CI.
- No measurable latency regression (>5%) for token registration in normal steady-state.
implementation_notes:
Files changed expected: control-plane/token_manager.go, control-plane/leader_rebind.go, control-plane/audit_enricher.go, control-plane/e2e/failover_test.go.
Key approach: use a reconciliation table persisted in etcd with TTL for in-flight unwrap correlation IDs. Token registration will perform an atomic write with the current leader vnode id; leader rebind will scan outstanding correlation entries and reconcile ownership. Audit path will subscribe to reconciliation completed events before deciding to drop fields.
